set_aside.subject: R0-86 import representation of an object
set_aside.text: R0-86 says "The import carries it inside its project", while R0-34 says an import "keeps its links: customer, object, rooms, pointers" and the primary import action promises projects "with their customers, objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact".
set_aside.question: Must the import represent the object only as embedded project data, with no object identity or link, and which identities and links does "ids kept, links intact" cover?
options: The object is embedded; only project, customer, room and pointer identities and their applicable links are kept
The import retains a distinct object link despite the object having no caller-visible id
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the object as embedded project data and preserve no distinct object identity or link.

set_aside.subject: R0-87 audit history after anonymisation
set_aside.text: R0-87 says "When it was archived and when it was anonymised, the audit log says", while R0-66 allows the owner to erase "every entry older than a date the owner gives" without exempting those entries.
set_aside.question: May the archive and anonymisation audit entries be erased under the ordinary audit-retention action, or must the audit log retain those dates for as long as the anonymised project remains?
options: They may be erased under R0-66, so the audit log states the dates only while those entries remain
Archive and anonymisation entries are exempt from audit erasure while the anonymised project remains
The dates must also be retained on the anonymised project before their audit entries may be erased
set_aside.default_guess: Apply R0-66 without an exemption and read R0-87 as describing the audit log only while its entries remain.
